notes.title: Rank: Warmaster Transparency Message for December 2nd, 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]

[h1][u][b]An open and honest letter of where are things and where are they going[/b][/u]
[/h1]

It’s the 2 year anniversary of the Early Access Release of Rank: Warmaster.  This letter is more a transparency of what is happening and what has happened.

[b]Short Answer:[/b]  We aren’t dead (mostly), and more updates will be coming just far less often than updates happened when they happened regularly.

[b]Long Answer:[/b]

[h2][u][b]The tragedies of the past year or so…[/b][/u]
[/h2]
As posted in previous updates, there has been a lot of personal tragedy during the development of this project.  Of the two programmers who worked on this project, Matt unfortunately died.  I am the lead dev, head programmer, and man of many hats running the studio.  Matt had been a close personal friend for well over a decade, so his loss hit me hard, and obviously greatly hurt the progress of this project.  

After the dust settled from that, it was decided that my efforts might be better served to develop a smaller game, based in the same universe.  The idea was that since Rank: Warmaster really didn’t gain the traction it needed because of it being our first commercial game, as well as not having the funding to advertise to a large enough audience to gain that traction, perhaps a less complicated game would gain the attention needed.  So Rank Warmaster: Bunker Buster was born.
  
It’s a tower defense game, using the same custom engine.  Part of the idea was as things were updated and fixed, it would flow back into Rank: Warmaster.  And that is what happened for quite a few months. You saw previous posts hinting at this new project.  Since most of the things needed to create such a project was already in existence as part of the current engine and game, it was felt it would be a quick project.  Unfortunately, as anyone knows in Game Dev, things rare work out as expected.

Only a month into the development, my father was in a car accident, and while surviving that initial injury, he slowly deteriorated over the following months.  I started to be responsible as power of attorney for his affairs before he passed, and then the executor of his estate after he passed.  Between being the executor and issues with my son also being in the hospital for unrelated things, I just didn’t get anything done for about 5 months.  I just couldn’t realistically, as much as I tried, to keep pace with the every two week release schedule that I had set for myself for Rank: Warmaster.  There just wasn’t anything of substance to release so I stopped, as you might have noticed.

[h2][u][b]Where things are going[/b][/u]
[/h2]

Things have finally settled down enough in the past month or so to get back to coding and Biz Dev and actually make progress.  And I am, and I have a lot of progress on Bunker Buster.  It will NOT be released into early access, since I don’t want to make that mistake again.  It will be a 1.0 to show what can be done.   All the things developed for Bunker Buster, if applicable, will be put in Rank: Warmaster.  The hope is after Bunker Buster is finished, that work will more directly resume on Rank: Warmaster to do a 1.0 release and get it out of Early Access.  In Effect, as a re-launch, hopefully.

The good news is more experienced people have been getting involved with Bunker Buster, so it should be a far more polished product than Rank: Warmaster has been.  With that experience the hope is to apply what was learned.  

I’m not going to set a release date for Bunker Buster but I do expect to have something for the public by first quarter next year.  Considering it’s December, that isn’t too long.

I do appreciate those that have stuck with the project through all of this, and it was very important to me that you knew Rank: Warmaster wasn’t abandoned.  And you deserved to know why the updates stopped and what was happening.  I do appreciate your understanding and patience.

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates May 28, 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for May 28th, 2023.  Things are still ramping back up from the hiatus from before.  In the previous release it was found the turrets weren't as accurate as one had hoped.  Testing found some flaws, which are now corrected.  

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/eacb163e6ad416b0a5060f29cb14b90af85ce0cd.jpg[/img]

The above screen shot more prove that the pulses are finally being accurate.  You can see the red trailing hit explosions as there are other shots incoming.  The previous release in certain circumstances the turret would not track correctly.  Interestingly, this actually ends up making the pulse turrets rather over powered because of the damage model.  Admittedly, if a ship is changing course regularly, because there is a lag from when a shot is firing and how long it takes to travel to the target, it can still miss.  However, that is the whole point of dodging.  

Basically, a lot of tweaks are going on behind the scenes, and I'm hoping an announcement can be made soon.  You can see hints above.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

Further updates to the AI are expected.  Some of the ship AI seems to be acting up, so I have to figure out why that is and fix it.  

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates May 13, 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for May 13th, 2023.  Things are still ramping back up from the hiatus from before.  The main change in this update is the pulse weapon turrets will properly lead their targets.  The minor parts have more to do with internal sorting routines having tweaks to make them work better.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
As things progress, more minor features are being fixed.  The big one in this case was the pulse turret AI actually leading their targets.  While leading their target has been implemented for the player for ages, the AI never used it.  It always just used the "beam" logic, where it simply faced the target directly.  When things are flying straight and coming directly at the firing weapon, this was fine, but obviously this isn't the normal circumstance.  Pulse weapons have always been more effective when they hit something because they do all their damage at once rather than having it spread across the armor as a beam weapon would do on a moving target.  The larger problem as, of course, being able to hit something with a pulse weapon is harder.  Targeting pips always has existed for the players, but the AI that aims turrets have always been oblivious.  In short, now pulse weapons are more effective, especially for ground turrets.

Another internal update was an issue with the internal sorting routine that handles a bunch of objects at once.  Basically, a lot of tweaks are going on behind the scenes.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

More discussions about making the UI for the RTS/Nav screen work better are in progress.  Hopefully something can be settled on by the next update.

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates April 29, 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for April 29th, 2023.  A progress update has been a long time coming, but it is here.  The main significant update is that Admirals can now be ordered to attack other fleets or cities.  Also, updates to the load/save system won't force a game restart when then internal structures get changes, so now updates between version shouldn't make your save games crash.  

[u][b]AI Updates[/b][/u]
There has been movement in the AI this release.  While it's been a long time coming, this is a BIG part of the AI helper system.   The Admirals now know how to attack cities and fleets.  Which means the enemy can now do this too.  But that means you can simply make an Admiral AI, and tell it to attack a city or ships, and then forget about it.  It will start to build ships based on the designs available (if you have any.  If not, it will request you design some).  It will build a combination of assault ships and salvage ships.  Once it has determined it has enough ships to do the job, it will order the ships to attack.  After the battle, the salvage ships will be on hand to clean up the mess to get extra resources.  

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
As a minor part of the update, save games now have a version code in them that is actually used now.  This means that older saves from a previous release won't crash the game if the save format happens to change.  I have always resisted changing certain internal structures of the game because I knew it would break people's save files.  The new addition should stop that from happening when enhancements happen.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

The Admiral AI needs a good shake down to make sure it is done.  So expect tweaks in the coming weeks.  Hopefully the usability issues in the RTS screen will now have time to be worked on.  

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates March 1, 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for March 1st, 2023.  Two significant updates this time.  The newer turret is finally in the system, with all the fixes that brings, and the Navigation/RTS screen now sports better effects with the atmospheric shader being used.  Also a bigger hint of up and coming announcements.

[u][b]GDC Travel[/b][/u]
We will be at GDC!  We'll have a booth #308 at Game Connection (which is in a different place than GDC) while we are there, so if you happen to be at GDC, please reach out!

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
For the longest time, the RTS/Navigation screen hasn't had most of the graphical improvement that the main simulation/piloting screen does.  This is mostly because the shader that does the pretty atmospheric effects doesn't play well with UI elements.  This isn't too much of a problem on the piloting screen, but made the RTS screen ugly to unusable in how it originally interacted with it.  That issue has now been fixed as shown:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/b9820d9d44fc31239941d5d5692b6da81953d7bf.jpg[/img]
There will be more graphical updates to come, to be sure.

Also, the newer turret model has finally been integrated into the system.  The turret model hasn't been upgraded in all this time because the original code was very much hard coded to how the original turret model was built.  The turrets are more complicated beasts than the other buildings because they have moving parts.  In this case a "base", a "post", and the guns.  The base doesn't move and that is what is in the ground, the post is the main body, and the guns are well...the guns.  A lot of work has been done to undo the hard coding.  In the process, a lot of the problems with the old turrets are now gone.  There is even support for different barrel configurations now.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/40e977750a4ee9705b491bbd376fadc230a0e61a.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
During the upgrades to the ground turrets, a lot of fixes were done.  One of the biggest is the pulse weapons on the turrets weren't working realistically.  Now they aim at a target at least.  More work needs to be done to apply the lead equation to where they should be aiming.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

While the Admiral AI was put on hold for internal reasons, however as you can see, work is still being done.  More work is being done on the RTS section of the game and likely to fix some usability problems.  Hopefully there will be time to address some of the Admiral issues as well.

[u][b]Hints of things coming[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/da8156da548a0c57f3e719700feac905f0448e13.jpg[/img]

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates December 20, 2022
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for December 20th, 2022, and the last update for year 2022.     The scouting command for the Admiral is fully operational.  There has also been some clean up and UI notification updates.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
Up to this point, messages between the AIs or even notifications while being produced when a new research is completed or when a ship is produced, mostly went unnoticed.  Now, they show up as objectives or notifications, and non-critical messages (such as notifications of something completed) will auto-delete themselves after a short period of time.  Requests from the AIs will now show up as Objectives to be completed, and will remain until they are completed.
 
[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/a0b1e6f4c44eafff8100c911c3e238c10d5d19c4.jpg[/img]

The above is the pathing of multiple scouts all completely generated from the Admiral AI being told to do the scouting for you.  These ever expanding series of patrol paths will keep an eye on their area of the planet to see what might cross their paths.  By searching, new nodes, cities, and other events await.  This is only the first implementation of what the Admiral AIs will be able to do for the player and the enemy.

To be clear, the larger glowing parts are cities, so it shows the scope of how much ground is being covered.  Because of this, the enemies are about to be pushed back out of immediate attack range soon (after the Admiral updates for attack cities are done).  At which point you and your enemies will have to find each other first. 

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

The holidays are upon us, which means people go on vacations.  While there will be some updates in the next few weeks, there won't be much.  Some of the icons are being updated, and I'm hoping a graphical update will happen but I wouldn't expect too much work to be done in the next two weeks over the holidays.

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

A lot has changed over this past year.  And a new milestone has been reached even in this update with the start of the addition of the AI helpers finally in the game.  

[u][b]Artistic Update: Past and Present[/b][/u]
A lot has changed even in the graphics over the past year.  Here is an example of a few screen shots from a year ago, with the current ones first and what it was a year ago:

As mentioned before, the idea always was to have AI helpers in the game since the game can get complicated.  The first glimmer of these has been implemented in the Admiral AI.  While the full capabilities of this has not been implemented yet, the Scout Duty command has now been hooked up.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/0605c3bf1999d1e5ad49cd2e3e7f6e4baaeb2799.jpg[/img]

You just made a scout ship design. The admiral will now proceed to order up new scouts if he has money and you have a factory. notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for November 22th, 2022, the second November newsletter.  The main topic is the AI, of course, but not in the way you might think.  The AI Helper system has started to be implemented!  More on that below.  

[u][b]AI Discussion[/b][/u]

Rank: Warmaster while a micro manager's dream was never meant to be only played that way.  Because of the many genres that are being put together, it can be overwhelming. The original intent was always to have AI helpers for the player, to offload some of the work the player may not wish to handle.  The game was always intended that different ranks were different roles to handle different aspects of the game.  The opposing AI already implements this, because each faction isn't simply one AI, but several working together.  A Mayor to build and maintain cities/installations, an Admiral to handle fleet orders such as scouting, cargo transport, and of course attack an defense.  During testing of the newer Admiral AI, it became more obvious that the time for the Helper AI interface was required to speed up testing.  While the newer Admiral AI isn't available in this build (because it needs more testing), the helper interface is.  

What does this mean?  It means if you go into the Asset screen, and click on "Create New AI", it will ask for a role you want this AI to have.  After it's creation, if you go to the Nav Screen, you'll see an avatar representation of that newly created AI that you can click on, and see it's commands.  Mayors and Admirals have different possible commands, so you can explore this preview in the new build now available.  Obviously, this won't be a preview for much longer.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

With the new AI-Helper interface, newer and more appropriate icons are in the works being created for the different commands.  More and more different AI abilities will become available to the player, so the AI development is in process.  

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for September 13th, 2022, the first September newsletter.  This update is a smaller update, mostly focusing on Steam multiplayer integration, better building information, and the turrets are now useful.  And as usual, there are more bug fixes and cleaning.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
Joining a multiplayer game would normally be difficult unless you were familiar with IP addresses, port forwarding and the difference between internal addresses and external ones.  This can get complicated for the average user.  We have mostly completed the multiplayer wrapper for Steam, that allows players to host a game on their machine.  Now a player can startup a server without the server worrying about their IP address or ports.  The steam Invite mechanism currently only partially works and we couldn't get it done for this release, however it's 90% there.  Once it is, you will be able to just join a friend's game easily via the steam interface or get invites from the server directly.  The invites from the server do work in the sense of being able to send invites to friends.

The Navigation screen has always been confusing around the buildings.  It can be hard to understand how much longer a building needs before it's completed, or even what it is doing.  Some buildings have been updated with more information in the popup information box.  For a turret, it will list what weapon it has, and who is it's target if any.  Turrets have also been made more powerful and actually effective.  This will likely go through a lot more balancing, but the ranges have greatly been increased, as well as damage.  Because of the internal changes, expect more diverse set of ground turrets coming.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/6a33c87edd2eac695568af997d11eef038fdc676.jpg[/img]

Just some turrets firing because they finally have range to hit something.

[u][b]AI Update[/b][/u]

Some minor fixes with the quick designer for the AIs.  Mostly fixing issues with ship hull selection and preventing crashes if a required part for a role type hasn't been researched yet.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

The steam wrapper for the integration is mostly complete, at least for the multiplayer.  Right now, it is a matter of fixing what happens when an invite reaches the client.  The data is good, but there is some minor issues that need to be correct for it to fully work on the client end.  The invite integration does work fine, and a lot of effort was put into getting a server seamlessly available to incoming players.  We hope that achievements can be added soon.  

On the AI front, it was noticed that sometimes AI players would just stop and not finish their base. 
 That has been corrected.  The steam integration and turrets no really working sidetracked the AI progress, but since both are solved, AI progress will resume.  

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates August 30, 2022
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for August 30th, 2022, the third August newsletter.  This update more concentrates on the RTS side of the game in the Navigation (Nav) Screen. 
 There have also been some audio voice over alerts added.  And as usual, there are more bug fixes and clean.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
There have been several significant additions to the Nav Screen.  First, is the ability to use the empty space to the right of the screen. This was, up to this point, walled out to be usefully clicked on because there were hidden controls there.  Now those controls no longer affect or stop the player's actions, which eliminates a lot of confusion.  The second major thing is control groups, which is standard in RTS games, but until now, was unimplemented in Rank: Warmaster.  Basically, any group of objects you have selected can now be put onto a hot key group by pressing CTRL and the hot key.  As an example CTRL-1.  Now if you simply press 1 from now on, it will automatically select the objects that were in that group.  Double pressing the key will center on those objects.  Do note that since the game doesn't allow objects that are selected to be off screen, it will automatically zoom out to display the objects selected.  This is likely to change in the future for a smoother transition.
The last major thing that was added by request was being able to use the left-click to place a building.  Normally one would select the build command for the builder bot, then the category of building and then the building itself.  Placement would normally by done with the right mouse button as execute (which still works).  However, many people felt that the left click should also be available for this use, so now it is.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/fdcc232020ffc28fe33b000b14cd3c4da3d8a6cb.jpg[/img]

As you can see, the building's glow can easily change based on the selected colors that they player or AI chooses.  More work is being done to enhance the individual ship hulls.  Watch for that soon!

[u][b]AI Update[/b][/u]

The enemy AI (and the player) now uses the same methods of designing a ship.  Which means the AI players' designs are more robust.  Also, the "default" button in the quick designer no longer creates a bare bones design, but a fleshed out one that can still be modified, of course.  This helps to stop really bad designs to be fielded by accident, especially for newer players who don't know what to modify yet.  One still has to pay attention to what is being created, however.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

The steam integration has hit a snag which is forcing us to reinvent the wheel in certain parts.  What this ends up meaning is that certain features will be in-game rather than in the Steam Overlay itself. 
 Achievements and other integration will be coming at some point, but the multiplayer joining/invite of a game is the highest priority.  We do, however, have a list of achievements finally, but they have yet to be implemented.  Now that the Design AI is in place for the Warmaster, work on the Admiral AI will begin, along with some tweaks to the Mayor AI.  Once the Admirals know about scouting, the enemy can finally be pushed back to more far away nodes, so the player will have to search for the enemy (as will the enemy search for the player).

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

Each screen has it's own real estate problems, and while efforts were made to keep the pop up locations reasonable, even if the player dragged things out of the way, the next pop up would simply return to the default position.  What is best for the player would change per screen, so now that is remembered per session.
Some other minor improvements is to the mouse wheel support, which now is more consistent and doesn't fight with the old drag and throw methods which are still there.  

The reload  should be more reliable from different screen saves.  A lot of smaller bug fixes and updates have been done across the various screens.  See the patch notes for such details.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for June 21th, 2022, the second June newsletter.  The big part of the update is the salvage system has been automated.  Of course a lot of work has been done on the tutorials, which have now been renamed.  

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
While salvage has been working for a while, it has never been automated.  Now if you a ship design with a cargo bay and salvage beam, you will be able to order it into salvage mode.  It will clean up the disabled ships on the battlefield from both sides, and return the salvaged RMs and CMs back to your warehouse automatically, and then wait for more!
The flight tutorial has been getting more polish, and the Basics tutorial that handles the RTS and 4X aspects of the game is on the verge of being playable all the way through.  So please try it and give some feedback!  Obviously a lot of polish need to be done.  Also some helpful minor updates are that disabled ships will just turn off their engines, rather than if their main engine still worked they would effectively run away, which made them harder to salvage.  Also loading a save from a different screen than the flight sim screen, you will return to that screen upon load.  The last more major update is the campaign now has useful and randomized defaults, including logos and colors for your corporation.  There is a longer list, if interested, please check the patch notes.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/f573f31db3f7c4e91d3ca19b49c4172496a68b0e.jpg[/img]
Here is a closer view of the newer buildings, showing some of the building tweaks.  Also, coloring of the different transport beams have been standardized.  Red for extracting resources from a building, purple for putting resources into a building, white for the builder beam, blue for repair, and green for mining or salvaging.  

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

Tutorial 2 is in the final push of getting it running.  It will need polish, but it will be functional and much of it already is.  The automated ship designer is likely to be worked on next to have the opponents makes more sense in their design.  Automated repair ship AI will come hopefully afterward.  As previously mentioned, the tutorials allow a lot of gameplay and shows what needs to be fixed or updated.  Sort of triage for a video game.  

That's all for this update, stay tuned for more news next time! If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for June 7th, 2022, the first June newsletter.  As usual, most of the updates are around the tutorials, however, tutorial 2 is about ready. 
 While not polished by any means, it at least can be completed (if the proper path is taken).  There has also been a graphical update on the buildings.  There are the typical bloom refinement and bugs fixes of course.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
The tutorials has been the main focus.  While Rank: Warmaster isn't hard to play or understand, especially if you've played the genres before, the controls may need a small refresher for how we defaulted the controls, and the progression of the game itself.  Also doing the tutorials show a lot of places polish and improves, and even bug fixes are needed, which is a lot of why they are taking as long as they are.  It's not so much putting in the dialog, but making sure what they are referring to is working correctly.  What came out in playtesting was how long it took to extract the resources to build a building wasn't needed or even planned to be that way. So now that is far quicker and therefore less annoying.  Many other flow issues switching between screens has been cleaned up, such as the building screen.  There is a far longer list, if interested, please check the patch notes.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/56ecb087e19a8e6cc431c1476abd93d479298fa2.jpg[/img]

The building bloom tweaks have started.  There are still a few things to iron out, of course, but the buildings do have a more sci-fi flare to them now.  Also the effects for moving resources have been standardized to take advantage of the new bloom effects, so extracting is red, placing is purple, mining/salvaging is green, and repairing is blue, with building still being white.  As a bug fix, we noticed that the building effects had stopped working in the Navigation screen, which of course is now fixed.
There will be further tweaks to the buildings, and the first round of updates to the ships should be coming soon.

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

Tutorial 2 needs a lot of polish and finishing touches.  The Quick Designer has a few paths through it in tutorial 2, and while the short path is usable, the longer and more in-depth still needs to be fleshed out.  The Salvaging AI is currently being worked on and should be expected in the next release.  What this will mean is you can make a cargo ship with salvage beams and order it to clean up the battlefield and it will do so on it's own, and drop off the cargo back at base or a local cargo ship or repair ship.  Automated repair ship AI will come afterward.  As previously mentioned, the tutorials allow a lot of gameplay and shows what needs to be fixed or updated.  Sort of triage for a video game.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/58c1d01d7d94901d9032a06564652ab0f243eb66.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for May 24th, 2022, the second May newsletter.  Most of the updates have been to the tutorials to make them explain things better, and fixing the problems that came up during testing.  Also some bloom refinement has been accomplished.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
The tutorials have been the main focus, as have been likely noticed.  A LOT of refinement has been done to Tutorial 1, to explain things better based on feedback, and now tutorial 2 is also getting that same treatment.  It can be amazing of all the small things that need to be updated and tweaked while polishing the tutorials.  Everything from commands not quite working right, to better explanations of concepts.  A good example is the addition of the feature of targeting an object in front of you.  This may sound useless, but it's very important in a dog fight when you have a better target of opportunity in front of you want you want to quickly switch targets to that ship!

A lot of bloom tweaks have been implemented.  Shields now have create a different glow about them, and they no longer block bloom effects like the sun or other light sources.  In the above screen shot, you can see a lot of personal battle damage on the shields, and the other ship has their shields being lowered from the reactor no longer working.

Buildings are being finalized with better emissive effects, and many of the ships have also been updated.  Expect those updates in the next release!

[u][b]Short-term RoadMap[/b][/u]

Tutorial 1's updates have been implemented and only a few tweaks are left.  We will see what the playtesters thinks about it.  Tutorial 2 is coming along nicely explaining research, building ships and a base, and even ship design.  While not yet completed, still covers a lot of gameplay ground.  While the tutorials are tested, a lot of minor (and major) bugs are being tracked and fixed.  So while the tutorials may seem to be taking a while, and they are, they are also acting as a quality assurance for the main game since the problems they find in the testing are being fixed one after another.

notes.content:

Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for May 10th, 2022, the first May newsletter.  The main update this time is an engine update to put a more modern version of bloom into the game. And it really makes a difference!

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]
The tutorials have been the main focus of late, and this update is no different.  Tutorial 2 is fully entered but still requires a lot of QA to make it considered complete.  A lot of work has been put in to making some of the instructions and where to click more obvious.  With integration with the new bloom implementation, this really has come out nicely. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/8cdfe0b8d3b020484c5d0d5511712517ece8c94c.jpg[/img]

The new version is for more impressive, as you can see above.  Even something as simple as engine plumes really standout now.  Emissive (light sources) on the buildings and ships look like they are supposed to, and even the look of the beams and pulses look much better.  As time goes on, tweaking will be done, of course, but it really is a impressive upgrade!

Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for March 1, 2022, the first March newsletter. Most of what to report is updates on what is already known.  The ability to customize a game is progressing.

[u][b]Quality of Life[/b][/u]

The ability to load and reload from story heavy scenarios has been added.  Before, the progress the player made during the tutorials couldn’t be saved correctly.  Now it can be.  While nothing is ever perfect, it is finally stable enough to be released.

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]

As a work in progress, we have a first look of our conversion to a PBR (Physical Based Rendering) to give the buildings and ships a better and more sci-fi look to them.  Below is a work in progress screenshot of an example we are working with.  This isn’t in engine, but we hope to have it look as good if not better in engine itself.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/7534a3e92087542b02590d8eb11fd19eab4fec70.png[/img]
Greetings, Warmasters and Candidates! This is the newsletter for February 15, 2022, the second February newsletter. Exciting news today as the game hits a new major milestone. As of today's release there will now be a limited form of the actual campaign available to be played. More on that below, we also have an artistic update from Paul this week.

[u][b]New Campaign Mode[/b][/u]

For the longest time the only playable options in the game were a few quick modes we were able to throw together that simply showcased some of the game's technical ability. As of today, players will actually be able to start a new game and use the Corporation Screen Matt has been working on for months to customize both the game settings as well as their corporation's bonuses, signature technology, name, and icon. To access this mode, simply select New Game from the main menu, then select Campaign. Use the Corporation Screen to select your starting options and once you click Done you will be dropped into a game. Ares will explain the rest from there.

The campaign will continue to evolve from this starting state as we add more features to the game and we'll keep you posted here as it takes on new and even better forms. We hope you like it!

[u][b]Artistic Update[/b][/u]

On another note, we have new ship models which Paul has been working hard to bring up to the current visual standard. The meshes for the ships are ready but they need improved normal maps and glow maps. For the less technically inclined, and those just interested in how this stuff works, normal maps are a way of adding details to an object without increasing the poly count. They include things like scratches, scuffed paint, and other extra details that would be a bit of a nightmare to add as part of the main mesh. There are three new models currently being worked on and we'll let you know more about that when they make it into the public release.

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates December 21, 2021
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/7534a3e92087542b02590d8eb11fd19eab4fec70.png[/img]
Greetings, Candidates! This is the newsletter for December 21, 2021, the second December newsletter. We have a quick statement at the top of this update: it is the holidays in the U.S. now, and many members of the team will be taking a vacation to spend time with family and recuperate from the pre-release rush. Because of this, there will not be a newsletter on January 4, and you can also expect a short period of lower responsiveness on the Discord and community forums. We will also not be releasing an update to the game at that time for the same reasons. You can expect things to return to a more normal state by mid-January, and we will still be around to keep track of any immediate issues that arise from today's update over the next week or so. Now, on to the actual news.

[u][b]Update Scheduling[/b][/u]

As hinted at above, we are planning to begin more regular updates to the game now that we have released in Early Access. These updates are planned to release every other Tuesday, alongside the Steam newsletter. Be sure to download the update in order to see the features described in the newsletters.

[u][b]Node Updates[/b][/u]

Our big feature update this time is the continued development of the node system. We recently placed nodes in the game as visible and targetable, now they actually have consequence. As of this update, it will be impossible to place mines off a node. This marks a huge turning point where one patch of Martian soil is no longer identical to any other, and there is a true reason for competition between corporations.

[u][b]Factory Repair[/b][/u]

Another big addition which we're excited about is the ability for factories to repair and rearm allied ships. In the new update, you will be able to command your ships to approach one of your factories, or pilot a ship close to a factory yourself, and the factory will automatically begin spending resources to repair those ships and refill all their ammo. Although ship-based repair is loosely covered in the first tutorial, we always wanted it to be a little more advanced to actually put a repair beam on a ship. At the start of the game, players will be dependent on having ships return to cities with factories for maintenance. Whether or not you prioritize unlocking repair beams for ships is entirely up to you and your own playstyle.

[u][b]Misc.[/b][/u]

We have also a few smaller items that don't really merit a big discussion.
-	The sound and notification system has been redone to prevent endlessly looping/repeating notifications
-	We have redesigned the keyboard controls for the Sim Screen to be based around the WASD keys in order to create a more intuitive control scheme
-	Jorden has begun drafting a new scenario called "Isolation", which is intended as a Mars scenario and is expected to be one of the longer scenarios a player can encounter in the early game

That's all for this update. It's been a very big year for us, and we're already so honored by the feedback we've been receiving. We have a long way to go yet, and we're listening closely to everything you've had to say to us. Happy New Year and Happy Holidays! We hope to see even more of you beginning your conquests of the solar system in 2022. If you'd like to give Rank: Warmaster a try for yourself, pick up a copy on Steam and begin your conquest of Mars! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1422270/Rank_Warmaster/

notes.title: Rank: Warmaster Post Release Retrospective
notes.content:
Greetings, Candidates! This is our first December newsletter, and also our first newsletter after we released in Early Access on Steam! To celebrate this occasion, and since the new year is just around the corner, we thought we'd break the mold and do a bit of a retrospective this time. Without further ado, let's take a look at some of the things we did in the last year!

[u][b]In no particular order, we:[/b][/u]

Completely rewrote the first two tutorials, heavily shifting the tone of the narrative and the characterization of Ares

Wrote the third tutorial, completing the basic writing for all of the tutorials needed to teach players the full game we have planned

Implemented the first tutorial almost fully, started on the second

Completely redid the UI in the Sim Screen

Created the new Corporation Screen from scratch

Created the new salvage, repair, and cargo system and have mostly implemented it now

Created and released out Steam page

Created and released two trailers

Redid large chunks of the tech web

Wrote several scenarios to spice up the mid-game action

Designed and implemented several new ship models

Redid the lighting system, upgrading it to Volume Tiled Forward Shading (VTFS) and made the game look truly splendid

Implemented early shadow maps to help with greater immersion

Upgraded the AI for the ships and AI controlled empires from "basic joke" to "now it can actually try to play the game"

We fixed countless bugs, crashes, exploits, and just weird interaction that defied categorization, reason, and physics

Released in Early Access on Steam, even though at times it felt impossible to actually achieve

[u][b]Now for some fun number dropping, just because we can:[/b][/u]

The scripts for all of the tutorials and scenarios, both finished and in progress, total 41,249 words

There is exactly 51 minutes of music in the game

And the whole game comes out to around 399,935 lines of code, give or take

We can't stress enough just how proud we are to have made it this far. We hope you're as excited as we are to see where we take the project in the future!

Greetings, Candidates! This is the newsletter for November 23, 2021, the second November update. We kind of liked the format from the last update, so we might stick with it for good. It also might not matter as much, but we're trying to be at least a [i]little[/i] consistent. The major topics for this update are nodes and scenarios.

[u][b]Nodes[/b][/u]

The progress on node implementation has come a lot further in the past couple of weeks. Where before the nodes were "in the system" but they didn't really have an effect, now you can actually see and target them.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/e93396ae3879ef1ec949c6d93c49d8311a400c50.jpg[/img]
[i]The pink sphere represents the center of the node, while the circle shows the node edges[/i]

They are visible in the Sim Screen and, when targeted, they show the amount of Ore remaining and a description of the associated node perk if there is one.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/e60bed5d0be9b77192dfa29271615b39a417de29.jpg[/img]
[i]Node info in the top left, these are test values and they are not a representation of the final version[/i]

We've discussed this other places but as a reminder, nodes sometimes carry perks in addition to being a supply of Ore. Those perks apply corporation wide bonuses to the corporation which controls the node so long as they have a fully powered, active mine on that node. This perk persists even when the node runs out of Ore, giving permanent incentive for corporations to maintain a presence on certain nodes long after they stop providing resources.

[u][b]Scenarios[/b][/u]

Scenarios are something which we've mentioned a few times broadly, and which come up regularly on Jorden's blog posts, but they are essentially events which occur in the game over the course of play. Their purpose is to break up the normal game loop by presenting the player with unusual situations. Most of them are short, but some have long lasting impacts on the game both narratively and mechanically. Jorden has recently begun integrating a few of the simpler scenarios into Articy where they can be imported to the game by Matt. There's still some infrastructure needed to really support them in the game itself, but this is an important first step in the process of transforming them from scripts written in Word to full-fledged game events ready for player experience. More on this as it develops further.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/6f516197546965c9ef6998e2a9456a40d4117b1e.jpg[/img]
[i]A look at our project list in Articy. we're so excited to share these stories with you![/i]

Greetings, Candidates! This is the newsletter for November 9, 2021, the first November update. We're breaking the format this time since we're still very deep in the trenches of polish and testing. Rather than go by person, we're going to cover the major topics of recent activities: the flight tutorial, polish and features, and the new trailer.

[u][b]The Tutorial[/b][/u]

While still being heavily tested, Tutorial 1 is currently coded in from start to finish. What this means is that all of the things that were written by Jorden have been, in some fashion, implemented by Matt. All that needs to be done is to crush all the bugs that come up as they are found until we have something worthy of public attention. Tutorial 2 has unfortunately been put on hold for the time while we attempt to properly implement more gameplay features.

[u][b]Polish and Features[/b][/u]

On the polish end, there has been a lot of adjustments to the piloting AI so that it better responds to commands from the Nav Screen as well as more dynamically reacting to situations in the world (such as suddenly coming under attack). Paul has also been doing a lot of great work on updating many of the screens in the game which were first designed... honestly, in some cases, the best measure of time is "they were designed a whole pandemic ago". More on that in Paul's [url=http://blog.rankwarmaster.com/index.php/ui-ux-artist-discord-button]last blog[/url] and [url=http://blog.rankwarmaster.com/index.php/ui-ux-artist-screen-review]the one before it[/url].

We're also implementing some more features which have been planned and needed for a long time, namely nodes and Travel Mode. Nodes are areas where Ore can be mined out of the ground (which is currently just "everywhere"). Their implementation gives players something to actually fight over and we're very happy to finally be getting them into the game. Travel Mode is an answer to the extremely vast distances of an actual scale planet. Using Travel Mode allows ships to go much faster than normal so that they can cross the distances between nodes (currently planned to be tens of thousands of nodes) in a reasonable time frame.

[u][b]New Trailer[/b][/u]

Yes! We're working on a new release trailer! What's the progress? It's already been written, recorded, and voiced (yes, there are voices in this one). As we speak, Chris is editing the footage together and we will hopefully have something to show soon. Greetings, Candidates! This is the newsletter for October 12, 2021, the first October update. Before we get into the specifics, we have a big announcement! Rank: Warmaster will be having a media release starting on October 15, just three days from now. What does this mean specifically? It means that an early build of the game will be released to select playtesters and media influencers on the 15th, which will finally allow us to get some outside feedback. We're working hard to try and make sure we have a good build for this release, keep an eye out for potential Rank: Warmaster gameplay footage in the coming weeks. That's all we can share with you regarding upcoming releases, so let's cover news from the team.

[u][b]From the coders[/b][/u]

Matt and Art are attacking on two fronts here. There is the continued progress on the implementation of the tutorials, mostly by Matt, and the fixing of a bug that has plagued us for a long time and which has kept all of our gameplay trapped at the North Pole of Mars, being tackled by Art.

For the tutorials, it's hard to get into specifics besides squashing what bugs arise and trying to keep the whole experience smooth. The majority of effort goes into writing code which helps the engine to react more dynamically to player action during the tutorials, as well as making it easy to point out the different areas of our HUD as they are taught. To put it more simply, Rank: Warmaster is a complex game and sometimes even simple objectives have multiple ways of being completed. The engine needs to be able to understand this and progress the dialogue of the tutorials appropriately.

As to the bug Art is working on, it basically comes down to "We're trying to get the game to understand that on a sphere (like a planet) "up" is relative." Until this is fixed, buildings not on the north pole are being built sideways because the game thinks "up" is above the pole. Naturally, this is a problem.

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

Jorden has been submerged in work on the tutorials. So has Matt. But on a couple of recent days Jorden came up for air and began writing out the larger campaign outline for the narrative of Rank: Warmaster. Not to say that there was never a plan for the story before, we've known for a while where the story was going to go, but actual details for the campaign at different stages of the game are being written. In addition, Jorden has begun writing the first campaign scenarios, the actual in-game situations which will allow the player to progress through Rank: Warmaster's story. More work is expected to be done on that as the tutorials become more and more stable, but unfortunately we are not expecting to have any mid-game scenarios implemented by the Early Access launch.

[u][b]From the artists[/b][/u]

Kathleen and Paul are hard at work putting together concepts for building lights, so that it can be made visually apparent when any given building is active by the patterns of lights on the outside. This also makes the buildings much more visually interesting.

[u][b]From our QA tester and game content designer[/b][/u]

Lastly is Adam, He of the Longest Title. Adam has been devoting his time to testing and re-testing the tutorials. This is meticulous work that will pay off heavily in the long run and we definitely need it as we approach our first release.

That's all for this update! A lot of interesting news and many challenges still in front of the team. Be on the lookout for more exciting news from us in the coming weeks, and we'll see you next time with another newsletter. The implementation of the tutorials is one of our final major obstacles before an early access release, and we're hoping to potentially have footage of one of the tutorials to show you all soon.

In addition to hooking up the Articy projects into the game, a process which requires individually adjusting several hundred dialogue elements total, Matt has also been getting further work done on the Corporation Screen and the capacitors interface. The new Corporation Screen was shown off in our last livestream, and the capacitors have featured a couple times now, but Matt and Paul have been working to implement a graphical update for the capacitor interface to make it more user-friendly, not to mention prettier. Results expected very soon!

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

Jorden happily reports that the first draft of Tutorial 3 has been fully written! In addition, the Articy integration of Tutorial 2, the actual moving of the script from Word into an Articy project that the coders can work with, is fully complete ahead of schedule. At current pace, Jorden expects to have Tutorial 3 integrated before the end of the week, then comes final revisions and the writing of voice scripts so that Ares can be voiced. All said and done, the narrative work is proceeding ahead of schedule.

[u][b]From our composer[/b][/u]

Finally, a quick sound update. We mentioned in the last update that Chris is recording the voice lines for Tutorial 1 at the moment, and that is coming along quite well. In addition to that, there is further progress on the game's next song as well as the addition of new weapon sound effects which are soon to be brought fully into the game.

That's all for this update! We'll be back in a couple weeks with more news. To keep up to date on our progress as well as to be notified as soon as the game is available, make sure to wishlist us on Steam! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1422270/Rank_Warmaster/

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/04b9f6accd6a90f44eb4f74528e8c889963a8ed2.png[/img]
Greetings, Candidates! This is the newsletter for August 31, 2021.

[u][b]From the coders[/b][/u]

We have two new features to discuss here. First is the creation of the research AI, which serves to allow the AI controlled corporations to make more interesting decisions regarding their research. We've mentioned the move from state machine AI to the IAUS model, but up until now we'd only gotten the Builder Bot properly working that way. The research AI is our first AI using this model that isn't centered around controlling a ship. Now the AI can pick research based on what it needs, as well as having preferences for certain technologies based on its personality.

The second feature is the new capacitors component for ships. The concept is that ship-based reactors are pretty expensive, both in terms of resources and available space. One of the first ways we tend to [strike]cut corners[/strike] improve design efficiency during live streams and testing is by reducing the size of the reactor. This provides the ship with less power to run all systems, but not all systems need to be run constantly. Now capacitors can be added into the ship for minimal extra space and cost and they allow you to operate at full power for brief periods. We're hoping that the expanded design options will lead to more interesting strategies during testing.

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

Following on the heels of the recently completed Tutorial 2 draft, the Tutorial 3 draft is now very nearly finished. The first two tutorials focused on familiarizing the player with singular aspects of the game, the flight simulator gameplay in Tutorial 1 and the city building and RTS gameplay in Tutorial 2. Tutorial 3 is designed to cover the broader elements of multitasking and managing all the elements introduced in the first two tutorials at the same time. You could say that the first two tutorials are designed as "How do I use the basic interfaces available to me?" while Tutorial 3 is more "OK, great, now how do I combine all this to actually play Rank: Warmaster?" Jorden is hoping to have the first draft for Tutorial 3 completed by mid-week and to begin working on the Articy Implementation for Tutorials 2 and 3 immediately after.

[u][b]From the artists[/b][/u]

As with anytime a new system is implemented, we have to make sure the UI for that system is both functional and visually pleasing. To that end, Paul has been working on the new UI for power ratios in the Quick Designer. This new UI is, of course, to allow the player to actually add capacitors to their ships effectively. More information and pictures can be seen in [url=http://blog.rankwarmaster.com/index.php/ui-ux-artist-quick-designer-1]Paul's most recent blog[/url].

[u][b]From our composer[/b][/u]

Did you know our game features voice-overs? If you've watched our livestreams, then you've already heard the voice of Ares as alerts come up, but we also have voice-overs planned for our tutorials and scenarios. All voices in Rank: Warmaster are either performed or created by Chris. We aren't certain yet to what degree the tutorials will be voiced by Early Access launch, but Chris has been working on recording the voice lines for Tutorial 1 so that you can at least hear some of what we have planned for the game. We very much hope you enjoy his performance as the voice of Ares as much as we do.

That's all for this update! Stay tuned for more information as our first newsletter of September will be in two weeks. To keep up to date on our progress as well as to be notified as soon as the game is available, make sure to wishlist us on Steam! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1422270/Rank_Warmaster/

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/04b9f6accd6a90f44eb4f74528e8c889963a8ed2.png[/img]
Greetings to our future Warmasters and Pilots! Just another quick update from the Rank: Warmaster team.

[u][b]From the coders[/b][/u]
After finishing implementing VTFS, and noticing an increase in frame rate, Art turned his attention to implementing cascading shadow maps. Shadow maps are actually exactly what they sound like, images that show how the shadows would be cast based on the light source. Because our map is very open it's difficult to create shadows that look good at all distances with only one map so the "cascade" part means we actually have several at different resolutions and which one you see depends on how far you are from that object or area. Tl;dr our terrain, ships, and buildings cast shadows now and it looks super cool. It also drops the frame rate just a little so, more work to be done there.
To finish the implementation of our new lighting Matt has been adjusting the code for our ship shader program. This will allow us to take the ship silhouettes we already have and add things like running lights wherever we want and on the fly. This helps to modernize our look without us having to completely re-render any of our models.

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

Jorden was away much of the past couple weeks but has returned and begun writing the new version of Tutorial 2. This tutorial will cover the basics of base building and fleet command which are necessary for the RTS elements of our game. Refinements on the salvage system are an ongoing process as well as implementing another of our screens, the Ship Detail Screen which is a secondary screen that pilots will use to examine the detailed conditions of their ships as well as customize aspects such as weapon fire groups and power distribution. In more fun news we’ve had a graphical breakthrough as Arthur has finished implementing VTFS, or Volume Tiled Forward Shading, which is a system to greatly improve the number of light sources our game can tolerate. With this we’re able to increase our limit from just over a hundred lights to thousands of lights without any notable loss of framerate.

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

Jorden has finished the writing and Articy implementation for the rewrite of Tutorial 1 which focuses on teaching players to act as pilots in our game. Tutorial 1 covers basic piloting and dogfighting as well as fleet command and distant surveying. For those of you most excited by the flight simulator aspects of our game, tutorial 1 should teach you everything you need to know to get into the skies and beyond.

[u][b]From the artists[/b][/u]

Kathleen has been putting together some of the first sketches that eventually become new ships in our game. We’re very excited to see what else she can bring to life. Meanwhile Paul continues to put together the new Corporation Screen. Once that’s in the game we’ll be able to allow players to decide the details of a game before they start and to genuinely feel like they’re playing their own corporation.

[u][b]From our QA and game content designer[/b][/u]

Finally, Adam has been putting together the details on some of the final elements of basic play such as sensor jammers and Builder Bot upgrades. The Fog of War and ship sensors have been implemented to require players to scout out enemy locations, now we just need to the other half in the form of jamming technology that players can use to stay hidden. notes.title: Rank: Warmaster News and Updates June 8 2021
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40466477/04b9f6accd6a90f44eb4f74528e8c889963a8ed2.png[/img]
Hello all and welcome to the very first Rank: Warmaster Steam Newsletter! We plan to use this space to bring updates on our progress every two weeks. Since this is the first newsletter it may run a little longer than the others since we have a little more to cover. We're very excited to start sharing updates through Steam so without further ado, let's jump into it.

[u][b]From the coders[/b][/u]

We've recently started using Articy: Draft 3 for our narrative scripting purposes. The intent is that this software will allow us to create and implement scenarios written by our content writer, Jorden, with a minimum of fuss. Naturally, just using the program doesn't create the scenarios in our game so the majority of Arthur's time in the past few weeks has been spent designing and implementing an import for Articy, which is just about done. This has also necessitated the creation of a new campaign engine for the game.

Previously scenarios (such as the tutorials) were created by first writing them up on our project wiki and then manually creating them in the game's scripting engine. The scripting engine is a very powerful and flexible tool, but inherently slow. Doing things this way was a ton of work at a glacial pace with a high rate of error. When the team got fed up with that they looked into new solutions. Articy and the campaign engine are specialized tools designed specifically around the narrative aspects of the game, or more specifically, the aspects of the game that aren't the direct results of player actions. In addition to being easier to work with directly, the campaign engine also runs much faster than the scripting engine allowing us to use the scripting engine in specific places where it is necessary rather than for the whole scenario.

At the same time, Matt has been focusing on adding some of the final, critical game mechanics needed to complete the core game loop. Namely the salvage, repair, and cargo systems are near-fully implemented into the game. It has always been our goal for salvage to be a critical aspect of Rank: Warmaster, both in the sense of reclaiming the resources lost when a ship goes down but also in the sense of stealing enemy wreckage to take their resources and gain insights into their technology. With salvage we can add a whole new layer into the game in which every conflict generates new resources to fight over, in the form of derelict ships. Regardless of how well the fight goes the matter is never fully resolved until the field is picked clean of all the leftovers and players should think twice before committing too many resources to a fight with poor odds of success. Since we always wanted salvaged resources to come back in the form of Component Materials (or CMs) this also made it necessary to actually bring CMs into the game for the first time as well as designing a proper cargo system for ships to carry these resources.

[u][b]From our content writer[/b][/u]

On the narrative side of development Jorden is working hard on ensuring that the tutorials and early scenarios of the game are entertaining. With Articy as a tool it should be much faster and easier to implement everything from the original outlines and more news is expected to come very soon. Jorden has also been working to improve the public face of Rank: Warmaster with adjustments to the Discord server and work on the script for our final launch trailer.

That's all we have for this first newsletter. Stay tuned for more updates on these aspects as well as progress from the rest of the team!
